newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Gecamines flying cobalt from ex-Zaire to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Gecamines flying cobalt from ex-Zaire to Europe.

text.p: Cobalt is being airfreighted from former Zaire to Europe in order to benefit from high prices, a senior Gecamines official told Reuters by phone from Lubumbashi.

"We are seeking to profit from high prices. Roads are too slow," said a marketing official speaking from the company's headquarters. The official said that it took about one month to export by road and sea to Europe but added that cobalt was still being taken by road to Johannesburg in South Africa - a 10 day journey.
"Flights (to Europe) began not long ago," said the official, adding that a plane could carry 30 tonnes.
But the official declined to say how much cobalt had been airfreighted or specify when flights started.
A shortage of nearby material has helped to underpin cobalt prices despite claims by consumers that prices were easing due to the ending of the seven-month civil war in former Zaire.

The official noted that prices were starting to fall. High grade cobalt was indicated at around $25.50 per pound on Wednesday against $19 in early 1997. Lower grade ingots were around $22.50, versus $18.50
